title: Halfspace intersections with large Gaussian surface area
statement:
There is a constant $c>0$ such that for every integer $m\ge2$, there are a dimension $n\ge0$, vectors $a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb R^n$, and thresholds $t_1,\ldots,t_m\in\mathbb R$ for which the intersection
\[A=\{x\in\mathbb R^n: a_j\cdot x\le t_j\text{ for every }j=1,\ldots,m\}\]
has Gaussian surface area at least $c\sqrt{\log m}$.
hypotheses_covered: there exist a dimension $n\ge0$, $m$ vectors in $\mathbb R^n$, and $m$ real thresholds
